Hi Peter,
We’re approaching the end of Care Workers Recognition Month, but that doesn't mean our celebration and acknowledgement of care workers has to end. Care workers are essential workers who deserve to be seen and valued every day of the year.
Check out these stories of appreciation for care workers from supporters and advocates around the country:
_“Bridget came into our lives at a time when we desperately needed good, reliable, compassionate care for our infant, and she did so with warmth and kindness and humor and compassion. People like her are stewards through life‘s most important, and most difficult moments. we are eternally grateful to her.”
\- Shayda N.

“[Haley] has been a perfect and compassionate caregiver for 3 years and is a jewel. She takes me to the doctor, gets my prescriptions, grocery store and most places that I need to go.”
\- Patty G.

“My beloved friend, neighbor and caregiver [Songün] helped me stay safe and cooked and cleaned for me when I fell down a flight of stairs and broke my nose, ankle and foot. She stayed with me in my home during the night, when I came home from the hospital... She is a beautiful person inside and out who gives her best to her family and friends.”
\- Rebecca B._
---

clean_body: Read these stories from supporters Become a Care in Action member today to help make our wins possible! * Hi Peter, We’re approaching the end of Care Workers Recognition Month, but that doesn't mean our celebration and acknowledgement of care workers has to end. Care workers are essential workers who deserve to be seen and valued every day of the year. Check out these stories of appreciation for care workers from supporters and advocates around the country: “Bridget came into our lives at a time when we desperately needed good, reliable, compassionate care for our infant, and she did so with warmth and kindness and humor and compassion. People like her are stewards through life‘s most important, and most difficult moments. we are eternally grateful to her.” \- Shayda N. “[Haley] has been a perfect and compassionate caregiver for 3 years and is a jewel. She takes me to the doctor, gets my prescriptions, grocery store and most places that I need to go.” \- Patty G. “My beloved friend, neighbor and caregiver [Songün] helped me stay safe and cooked and cleaned for me when I fell down a flight of stairs and broke my nose, ankle and foot. She stayed with me in my home during the night, when I came home from the hospital... She is a beautiful person inside and out who gives her best to her family and friends.” \- Rebecca B. Workers like Bridget, Haley, and Songün do the critical work of looking after our loved ones every day — but too often, their work isn’t considered “real work,” and they often face discrimination and lower wages, which both affects workers’ personal lives and access to quality, affordable care for families. Our partner organization, the National Domestic Workers Alliance, collected these stories honoring workers and their contributions to our lives and our economy; And you can help us turn out voters, elect Care Champions, and enact care legislation that will lift care workers, by becoming a Care in Action member! In solidarity, Care in Action

Early voting in these local elections began yesterday, and it’s crucial that you remain vigilant and dedicated to electing candidates who will remain steadfast in their commitment to protecting your medical liberty, even in situations of declared emergencies or disasters. Team TFVC encourages you to visit your county’s election department to view your sample ballot, reach out to those who are running in your local races and ask them where they stand on the issues of informed consent, medical privacy and vaccine choice, and cast your votes accordingly! As a reminder, Early Voting is now through April 27, as well as April 29 and 30. Election Day is May 4. That's what I'm doing every day in the Senate. **I'm fighting for the Dignity of Work. **No matter where you're from or what kind of work you do, hard work should pay off for everyone. Whether you punch a clock or swipe a badge, earn a salary or make tips, are raising children or caring for an aging parent, I'll fight for you. **I'm fighting for accountability.** For years, we've seen corporations lobby for tax breaks and bad trade deals that hurt workers. I'm not afraid to stand up to Wall Street or take on Big Pharma to level the playing field. **I'm fighting for our fundamental rights.** My opponent has made it clear he doesn't have our best interests at heart. I will always fight for a more equal and inclusive country. **But here's the deal, Peter,** I need you to fight with me. This disappointing decision strikes another severe blow to our national security and undermines the rule of law. Mayorkas's actions,_or lack thereof_ , have directly contributed to the chaos and insecurity plaguing our border communities — including Arizona’s 6th District. As members of the communities living on the front lines, we witness the devastating reality of an uncontrolled border in our everyday lives. The immediate dismissal of these articles is unacceptable; it is an outright betrayal of the safety and well-being of our community. We cannot afford to turn a blind eye to misconduct within the highest levels of government, especially when the consequences are felt so acutely in our communities.

It is imperative that we stand up against this gross injustice and demand transparency and accountability from our government leaders.
I urge you to join me in speaking out against this injustice and demanding transparency and accountability in our government. Together, we can ensure that the voices of our communities are heard and that our leaders are held accountable for their actions.
Thank you for your continued support. Juan

body:
“If you want more young people in office, why do you support Joe Biden?”
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240423-1&t=1&akid=600%2E587540%2ElmqOQl)
Peter,
Since we launched Leaders We Deserve last year, there is one question that I keep getting asked. It’s a question I’ve been getting asked regularly since I started my activism with March For Our Lives, where we were an organization run by young people.
_“If you want more young people in office, why do you support Joe Biden?"_
**Leaders We Deserve is not about young people vs. old people — it’s always been about making sure Gen Z and Millennials have representation that reflects that we make up a third of the country’s population.**
In fact, throughout our country’s history, we’ve had a number of leaders who are remembered as being an older person, but started their activism at a young age.
These are exactly the kind of folks we want to elect more of: People like John Lewis, who ran for office as a young person on a mission to make urgently needed change, and ended up being one of the most important and effective leaders we’ve ever had in our country.
[**Our mission is simple: elect more young leaders who can bring important new perspectives to our government. If you’d like to help, you can pitch in $5 to support our work by clicking here.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240423-1?refcode=em20240423-1&amount=5&refcode2=600_587540_lmqOQl&akid=600%2E587540%2ElmqOQl)
The reality is that there have always been too many barriers to entry in public service in order to elect young leaders in the numbers we deserve, and our organization was founded precisely to help young candidates overcome those barriers.
After devastating losses in 2016, the blue wave in 2018 brought the Democratic Party a new appreciation for the impact young people can make at the polls. Then in 2020, Joe Biden was elected thanks in large part to huge turnout from Millennial and Gen Z voters — a leader who started his career incredibly young at just 29 in the Senate and has morphed into one of the most effective presidents of my lifetime so far.
I believe the decades of experience he has in the Senate plus his perseverance through major personal loss has made him so empathic and successful at passing major climate, infrastructure, and gun safety legislation with razor thin margins.
In 2022, young people reaffirmed our power at the ballot box, turning out in big numbers once again to hold off the much-touted “red wave” that never materialized. Newly elected young folks like Justin Jones in Tennessee and Maxwell Frost in Florida made waves. We also elected our first Leaders We Deserve endorsed candidate: Nadarius Clark in Virginia!
**It’s not just Gen Z and Millennials who stand to benefit from electing more young people, it’s the entire country and our future. Starting young takes advantage of the most powerful thing anyone can have on their side in politics: time. Gen Z will outlive most people on Capitol Hill, the question is how soon we can come into power.**
[**If you’re with us in this fight and want to make sure we can elect more of the leaders we deserve in 2024 and beyond, pitch in $5 or any amount you can to help support our work.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240423-1?refcode=em20240423-1&amount=5&refcode2=600_587540_lmqOQl&akid=600%2E587540%2ElmqOQl)

More updates soon,
David Hogg

body:
These figures explain why our work on college campuses is so important.
#
I want to make sure you saw these numbers on youth voter registration and turnout rates in Texas. They make the case for why Powered by People’s work on college campuses is so essential.
In the last election, less than 40% of 18-24 year-olds in Texas were registered to vote. And of those who were registered, less than half actually cast a ballot. Some deeply troubling figures considering that these young people are the future of our state.
But when you remember that Republican state leaders have banned online voter registration, removed early polling places from college campuses, and prevented young people from using their student IDs to vote, these numbers start to make sense.
That’s why Powered by People volunteers are on college campuses every day registering young voters, helping them navigate Texas’ voter suppression laws, and ensuring they have all the information they need to cast a ballot in November.

Hi Peter,
Today marks 14 years since those who would now be considered AZ MAGA Republicans signed S.B. 1070, the notorious “show me your papers” bill, into law in Arizona.
It allowed law enforcement officers to demand ‘papers’ and investigate a person's immigration status if they suspected a person was undocumented. Immigrants who failed to carry federal registration papers were guilty of a state crime. We all knew what this meant in practice. If you had dark skin and looked like ‘you didn’t belong,’ they ensured you knew it and would pay . This led to numerous cases of racial profiling, unlawful arrest, and family separation.
My friend Liz’s family was directly impacted by this law when her father was arrested at a park for failure to provide identification and then spent months in a detention center.
But when S.B. 1070 was signed, we didn’t give up – we got to work.
We came together: Democrats, Republicans, Independents, Latinos, People of Color, union members, educators, and youth activists. We spent countless nights and days outside the AZ State Capitol in protest, organizing, praying, hosting press conferences, fasting, marching, and strategizing to build political power so laws like this don’t happen again.
Since then, we have built strong and broad coalitions to fight back and have changed the political landscape of Arizona, with many of those youth activists now leading their own organizations.
I am proud to have been part of that change. I am proud to have led efforts to oust the author of SB 1070, Russell Pearce, and to have led the movement to oust the notorious Sheriff Arpaio, and I am proud that was the same coalition — growing larger each year — that came together to reject Donald Trump, Kari Lake, and extremists throughout our state in 2022 when I led the Arizona Democratic Party.
This same coalition needs to come together once again for us to win in Arizona’s third district and beyond. To elect Ruben Gallego to the U.S. Senate, re-elect Joe Biden and Kamala Harris to the White House, and pass an amendment to protect abortion rights in Arizona.
Will you join us by pitching in $20 or whatever you can afford today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftteran?refcode=X_042324_sb1070anniversary&amount=20]

#
Friend of life,

As you read this email, a precious preborn baby is about to lose his or her life through abortion. Despite the end of _Roe v. Wade_ almost two years ago, abortion rates are _increasing_.

The daily death toll of abortion is 2,813 in the United States -- that's 117 abortions per hour, 1.9 per minute, and one every 31 seconds.

The U.S. Supreme Court didn't end abortion. Congress has refused to stop the spread of this killing. But you CAN do something right now that will help turn the tide and save lives.

Live Action has the content proven to change minds about abortion and save lives, but we need to reach mothers who are moments away from abortion, especially in the most pro-abortion states.

We cannot reach these mothers - and those who influence them - without the caring support of people like you who invest daily in ending abortion. **Specifically, we are looking for 25 pro-life people in your state to give just $50 today. Your gift will fund:**
* The creation and release of _Truth about Sex_ videos and resources to empower young women and men to discover their own dignity and make life-affirming, healthy choices
* The ability to reach pregnant mothers with the _Window to the Womb_ web app that brings the life-saving power of 3D fetal development imagery into their pockets, showing how the precious preborn child is growing, learning, and playing in the womb.
* Providing local pregnancy centers with tangible support like diapers while mobilizing pro-life people to end abortion in their communities.

We cannot rely on someone else getting involved to help end abortion. It is up to us to lean in, invest, and save lives.

Here's your secure link to make your gift and help save a baby: **[https://give.liveaction.org/your-gift-will-save-lives-from-abortion/](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=2c6155211181448abcc51882a2b54b5e&_e=Z4fA8SopXfP5j2jDrlW6hAcUjVGmlsVCCCp-E1zZCg6SozG9m9aY4EzjHTSgChUIP3T8fcHubhs-fzzB4wyyaojeh7mV3JkP53zRNtmFQbju18tyT9bpKKLTMBBeJ7HlFkZFup4rE2N8V13fNfkMjfwfkW_WI6xQh1jszL_oBhV7-TeO04OltBBBEwHFMabdOGO0Jom64mkj9Ummqube_ohDdIPepZ__0uFnHftKgILKc0kSEkQanckx_62T2E1f03HdwK5SlBKDtB4_TcmHQAxV2oj0HCGMgaHJNwB10fs_XtcdfcvFix-EgMTREEKuESfvtWvfRIV2Zpd4tRgZjayhwcInoUB2HL5PsBd51_UcE-5fTg-NehQ52L5r3Czi7CMfLS7H8oHyHeomjsX32FeFBo48a0ErlPsby624BmM%3D)**

Thank you for speaking for those who cannot speak for themselves.

For Life,

Lila Rose

** Ben Toma's family legally immigrated to the United States when he was just 9 years old. His family fled the dangers of communism at the time in Romania to seek freedom and build a new life here in America.

subject: Honor Our Military Families in the Month of the Military Child
body:
Join the Team

| | | | | | | |
---
| | | |
---
| | | **Honor Our Military Families in the Month of the Military Child**
---

Dear Peter,
April marks the Month of the Military Child, a time to acknowledge and celebrate the resilience and strength of the children of our servicemen and women. These young heroes face unique challenges with grace, from frequent moves to handling long periods away from their parents. In Washington's 8th district, we are especially proud to honor their sacrifices and support their families.
My children were born and raised in the military as their father served our country. They were able to watch their dad put on the uniform that stands for freedom and go out to protect our rights. My campaign is dedicated to ensuring that the children of our service members receive the resources and support they need to thrive. This includes enhancing educational opportunities, providing better healthcare, and ensuring robust community support systems.
---
| | | |
---
| We ask you to join us in this cause by making a donation this April. Your contribution, whether $25, $50, or $100, will help us advocate for policies that uplift our military families and address the unique needs of their children.

---

Thank you for standing with us and recognizing the courage of these incredible children.

With gratitude,

Team Carmen Goers

# [Tell the Supreme Court: Don't delay, rule against Trump immunity now!](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te3a6219a-e330-458a-ad14-8fa79a66fd52/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

---
| | | The Supreme Court will decide whether Trump has immunity from criminal prosecution for the crimes he committed while he was president. They'll begin hearing arguments later this month, and [we need them to make a decision as quickly as humanly possible.](https://default.salsalabs.org/Td0146748-b0f9-41b5-aecf-4228081d9ba3/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) The Supreme Court's decision on Trump's immunity has massive implications. Any delay in this decision could push Trump's Jan 6 trial further back, allowing the possibility for Trump to win the election and pardon himself. That's not a risk our country can afford to take. This is an open-and-shut case! Trump's claim that he has full immunity for any crime committed is absurd and wildly dangerous. The Supreme Court must rule that Trump is not immune, and they must do it immediately. [**Tell the Supreme Court: Don't delay, rule against Trump immunity now!**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tea4d339a-6bfc-4532-9a1f-8e10f4722a3d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

body:
And doing better for our communities.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/421?t=1&akid=1172%2E62735%2EhFXXZW)
Peter — I want to talk to you about the fight for environmental justice. I’ve got a lot to say about this but the bottom line is this: The climate crisis is here — and our most vulnerable communities are the ones picking up the pieces. Congress needs to do more, and fast. **[Add your name here if you agree.](https://act.hillharper.com/survey/em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324/?source=em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324&t=2&akid=1172%2E62735%2EhFXXZW)**
**[SIGN THE PETITION »](https://act.hillharper.com/survey/em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324/?source=em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324&t=3&akid=1172%2E62735%2EhFXXZW)**
By now, most people in the country have heard of Flint, Michigan. Over the past few years, I’ve spent a lot of time in Flint — both as a Senate candidate and as an activist. The people I met there are resilient, and they have so much love for their community and their neighbors. But let’s be clear: Flint is also one of the poorest cities in America — over 40% of the people who live in the city live below the poverty line, and most of those are Black and Brown women, single moms, and working people just trying to provide for their families.
**A whole city was being poisoned, and our elected officials in Washington weren’t doing a damn thing to stop it.** When COVID hit, the crisis went from bad to worse. Flint residents were left without clean water at a time when hygiene and cleanliness were national imperatives. I couldn’t sit by and watch it happen.
I was invited to join a community event in Flint to raise money and awareness about the issue, and I remember talking to a man who told me _Hill, people love to come in and take selfies, but then we never see them again. Promise me you’ll come back._
With the help of social media and some incredible partner organizations, myself along with Iyanla Vanzant were able to raise over $60,000 to send 5,000+ gallons of clean water to Flint at the height of the pandemic.
But I want to do more, Peter. Crises like Flint are happening across this country, and our elected leaders in Washington aren’t doing enough to mitigate them. **That’s why, as the people’s candidate for Senate in Michigan, I’m championing an unapologetic and aggressive climate strategy that puts our communities first:**
* We demand a **transition to 100% clean electricity by 2035**
* We demand **robust financial support for global climate initiatives, like the Green Climate Fund**
* We demand **strict regulations to end price gouging at the pump**
* We demand **environmental justice for all** — that means putting frontline communities like Flint at the center of all efforts to confront climate change

This Earth Month, I’m calling on our leaders to get serious about this crisis — and I hope you’ll stand with me, Peter.
**[Sign our petition demanding Congress take immediate, substantial action to combat climate change. Let's send a clear message: half-measures and delays are unacceptable. We need bold action, and we need it now.](https://act.hillharper.com/survey/em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324/?source=em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324&t=4&akid=1172%2E62735%2EhFXXZW)**
**[SIGN THE PETITION »](https://act.hillharper.com/survey/em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324/?source=em_HHR_PET_EarthMonth_042324&t=5&akid=1172%2E62735%2EhFXXZW)**
Thank you for your action, your passion, and your commitment to our people and our planet.
In solidarity,
Hill Harper
Democrat for U.S. Senate

Flint residents were left without clean water at a time when hygiene and cleanliness were national imperatives. I couldn’t sit by and watch it happen. I was invited to join a community event in Flint to raise money and awareness about the issue, and I remember talking to a man who told me Hill, people love to come in and take selfies, but then we never see them again. Promise me you’ll come back. With the help of social media and some incredible partner organizations, myself along with Iyanla Vanzant were able to raise over $60,000 to send 5,000+ gallons of clean water to Flint at the height of the pandemic. But I want to do more, Peter. Crises like Flint are happening across this country, and our elected leaders in Washington aren’t doing enough to mitigate them. That’s why, as the people’s candidate for Senate in Michigan, I’m championing an unapologetic and aggressive climate strategy that puts our communities first: We demand a transition to 100% clean electricity by 2035 We demand robust financial support for global climate initiatives, like the Green Climate Fund We demand strict regulations to end price gouging at the pump We demand environmental justice for all — that means putting frontline communities like Flint at the center of all efforts to confront climate change This Earth Month, I’m calling on our leaders to get serious about this crisis — and I hope you’ll stand with me, Peter. Thank you for your action, your passion, and your commitment to our people and our planet. In solidarity, Hill Harper Democrat for U.S. Senate

Friend, Last week, our Congressional Mamas’ Caucus recognized Black Maternal Health Week with advocates and allies who are trying to eradicate racial disparities in our healthcare system. **Our country is facing an urgent maternal health crisis, with Black women particularly impacted** —being 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. I founded the Congressional Mamas Caucus with Detroit-based Mothering Justice to advocate for mothers of color and working class families who have too often been underserved by our government. We’re pushing for policies including affordable childcare, paid family leave, reproductive justice, and Black maternal health—such as the comprehensive _Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act_. From: **Rashida Tlaib******
Date: Mon, Apr 22, 2024
Subject: Sign to support the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act
To: dpwillis67@gmail.com
Friend,
We’re in a maternal health crisis: the United States maternal mortality rate is rising, and Black women are 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women.
Black women have been systematically neglected and mistreated in our healthcare system, and they’re also more likely to live with health conditions from air and water pollution.
I’ve been discussing these urgent challenges with colleagues and advocates during the past week’s Black Maternal Health Week. **As part of advocating to dismantle the systematic racism in our healthcare system, I’m urging Congress to pass the**** _Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act_****.**
This legislative package includes 13 bills that would:
* Extend WIC eligibility during postpartum and breastfeeding periods to provide crucial nutrition for parents and babies
* Support anti-bias trainings for employees in maternity care settings and establish Respectful Maternity Care Compliance Programs to address racism and promote accountability
* Expand access to high-quality maternal mental health care and substance use services
* Increase the number of nurses, midwives, physician assistants, doulas, and other perinatal health workers who moms can trust throughout their pregnancies, labor and delivery, and the postpartum period
* Improve maternal healthcare and support for incarcerated moms, including ending the horrific process of shackling people as they give birth
* Invest in community-based initiatives to reduce levels of and exposure to pollution and climate change-related risks
* Fund community-based organizations and Tribal organizations working on maternal health

Most pregnancy-related deaths are preventable, and it’s urgent that we implement these solutions to save lives now.

clean_body: We’re in a maternal health crisis, particularly for Black women and babies. | | | Friend, Last week, our Congressional Mamas’ Caucus recognized Black Maternal Health Week with advocates and allies who are trying to eradicate racial disparities in our healthcare system. Our country is facing an urgent maternal health crisis, with Black women particularly impacted —being 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. I founded the Congressional Mamas Caucus with Detroit-based Mothering Justice to advocate for mothers of color and working class families who have too often been underserved by our government. We’re pushing for policies including affordable childcare, paid family leave, reproductive justice, and Black maternal health—such as the comprehensive Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act. | Thank you for supporting life-affirming policies that help dismantle systemic racism. In solidarity, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib** Date: Mon, Apr 22, 2024 Subject: Sign to support the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, We’re in a maternal health crisis: the United States maternal mortality rate is rising, and Black women are 3 to 4 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women. Black women have been systematically neglected and mistreated in our healthcare system, and they’re also more likely to live with health conditions from air and water pollution. I’ve been discussing these urgent challenges with colleagues and advocates during the past week’s Black Maternal Health Week. As part of advocating to dismantle the systematic racism in our healthcare system, I’m urging Congress to pass the** Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act. This legislative package includes 13 bills that would: Extend WIC eligibility during postpartum and breastfeeding periods to provide crucial nutrition for parents and babies Support anti-bias trainings for employees in maternity care settings and establish Respectful Maternity Care Compliance Programs to address racism and promote accountability Expand access to high-quality maternal mental health care and substance use services Increase the number of nurses, midwives, physician assistants, doulas, and other perinatal health workers who moms can trust throughout their pregnancies, labor and delivery, and the postpartum period Improve maternal healthcare and support for incarcerated moms, including ending the horrific process of shackling people as they give birth Invest in community-based initiatives to reduce levels of and exposure to pollution and climate change-related risks Fund community-based organizations and Tribal organizations working on maternal health Most pregnancy-related deaths are preventable, and it’s urgent that we implement these solutions to save lives now. In Michigan, lawmakers have also introduced the “MI Momnibus” bill package to improve healthcare quality, access, and outcomes for Black women and birthing people in our state. Across the country, we will continue the push to eradicate racial disparities in maternal and infant health, and to dismantle systemic racism in all our institutions. Our team delivered the petitions to the Board of Elections three weeks ago, and now we're officially on the ballot to beat AOC in the Democratic Primary this summer. Dear Peter,

We thought you may be interested to receive this exclusive story from Illinois Review (https://www.illinoisreview.com/?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d11acbae2f-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) concerning the recent election for Cook County GOP Chairman.

** EXCLUSIVE: Dr. Eric Wallace Issues Statement Thanking Supporters, Todd Ricketts – Promises to Help Rebuild GOP, Support Conservative Candidates (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/exclusive-dr-eric-wallace-issues-statement-thanking-supporters-todd-ricketts-promises-to-help-rebuild-gop-support-conservative-candidates.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d11acbae2f-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
------------------------------------------------------------
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/exclusive-dr-eric-wallace-issues-statement-thanking-supporters-todd-ricketts-promises-to-help-rebuild-gop-support-conservative-candidates.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d11acbae2f-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D

By Illinois Review

On Tuesday, former candidate for Cook County Republican Party Chairman Dr. Eric Wallace issued a statement thanking supporters, including Chicago Cubs co-owner Todd Ricketts, who endorsed his candidacy and sent shockwaves across Illinois political circles.

In the one-page letter, shared exclusively with this publication, Dr. Wallace wrote,
CLICK TO READ FULL ARTICLE (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/exclusive-dr-eric-wallace-issues-statement-thanking-supporters-todd-ricketts-promises-to-help-rebuild-gop-support-conservative-candidates.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d11acbae2f-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/04/exclusive-dr-eric-wallace-issues-statement-thanking-supporters-todd-ricketts-promises-to-help-rebuild-gop-support-conservative-candidates.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d11acbae2f-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D

“I am deeply grateful to the ward and township committeemen who supported my candidacy for Chairman of Cook County Republicans. Our shared vision for a more competitive political landscape in our state, county, and the city of Chicago is a testament to our unity and commitment.”

Wallace also made a point that he wanted to play a role in helping to rebuild a broken Illinois Republican Party and away from “one-party rule” writing,

“I believe that, together, we can bring substantive change to Cook County wards and townships through candidate training and vetting, voter engagement, and fundraising to support the Republican Party and the communities we serve. I look forward to seeing the transformation of our communities through our hard work as we execute a comprehensive strategy to wrestle Cook County away from one-party rule.”

The former pastor and conservative activist then thanked Ricketts for his support.

* * *
**Georgia’s Legislative Session**
At the end of March, Georgia's MAGA-led legislature pushed through numerous bills targeting voters, immigrants, and our public schools. House Bill 976 and some provisions of Senate Bill 221 merged with SB 189 to form an omnibus proposal which could have the effect of disenfranchising Black and brown voters, seniors, students, rural voters, and Georgia's unhoused population. This bill complicates the voting process, overburdens election staff, and elevates the power of election deniers. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/83595480/468898107/1035750623?refcode=bsc_emm_ffa_20240423_f_Q1Recap_v1s1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOGFhOGJjZC1iZTAxLWVmMTEtYWFmMC03YzFlNTIxNGRhZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pHZIhbJHKVpaIO9ekErk1qa8yOOB8XhuLIHOB6_EYp0=)

Fair Fight Action founder Stacey Abrams was a recent guest on MSNBC, breaking down why fighting for democracy is at the core of our mission and the importance of connecting the dots around voting. We know that you’re busy too, so we’ve rounded up some recent news and information you might have missed: Georgia’s Legislative Session At the end of March, Georgia's MAGA-led legislature pushed through numerous bills targeting voters, immigrants, and our public schools. House Bill 976 and some provisions of Senate Bill 221 merged with SB 189 to form an omnibus proposal which could have the effect of disenfranchising Black and brown voters, seniors, students, rural voters, and Georgia's unhoused population. This bill complicates the voting process, overburdens election staff, and elevates the power of election deniers. | = Governor Brian Kemp can veto SB 189 and the other harmful bills from this past session, but we need to apply pressure — call him at 404-656-1776 before May 7 and demand he veto these attacks on Georgians’ fundamental freedoms. body:
Abortion rights are on the ballot in November.

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83595728/468899080/-247205437?refcode=BLU_EM_EMRG_2024-04-23_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkVNUi8xLzgxMzIxIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjkzMDg4NzdlLWJmMDEtZWYxMS1hYWYwLTdjMWU1MjE0ZGFkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=9XgkQYYcxvmbllAi5cabO_VWBvt6Ri15Z3zMoqzW0XA=)
---
| Peter,

Here are some things MAGA leader Donald Trump has said about abortion:
1. Trump believes abortion laws should be left to the states.

2. He also says that the states should _“do the right thing”_ – aka restrict abortion access.

3. He took the opportunity to claim he was “proudly the person responsible” for overturning _Roe v. Wade._

4. In the past, Trump has called for a national 16-week ban, and in his current race for president he has not backed down from that call.

I love to get lost in nature — literally. Back in the 80s, I once got separated from my hiking partner and ended up spending an unexpected night alone in Sequoia National Forest. While it wasn’t the adventure I had _planned,_ it certainly deepened my appreciation for our national parks. But you don’t have to get lost in one to understand the awe-inspiring beauty these parks hold. From the towering cliffs and waterfalls of Yosemite to the rugged coastline of Acadia, our national parks are irreplaceable treasures. These parks belong to all of us, offering every American a place of refuge and solace. **Yet the survival of these sanctuaries is under threat.** [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83595781/468899332/2105508926?refcode=ea.e98b1ec6-bf01-ef11-aaf0-7c1e5214dad0&ms=ea.e98b1ec6-bf01-ef11-aaf0-7c1e5214dad0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU5OGIxZWM2LWJmMDEtZWYxMS1hYWYwLTdjMWU1MjE0ZGFkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=EZy_Ljip_8MFRLE2Ss-mLOQe619B9MiphzEhbt5BI94=) Oil drilling, pipeline construction, and mining from the encroaching fossil fuel industry degrade air quality, disrupt fragile ecosystems and wildlife habitats, and ruin the natural beauty we cherish. The air quality in Rocky Mountain National Park has deteriorated, and the migration routes of mule deer in Grand Teton National Park have been disrupted, both directly linked to nearby oil and gas operations. Iconic sites like Glacier National Park in Montana are seeing their glaciers melt away and could disappear within 30 years. Yellowstone and Rocky Mountain National Parks are facing increasingly severe wildfires that threaten their landscapes and ecosystems. Mesa Verde in Colorado suffers as drought and wildfires accelerated by climate change threaten the preservation of cultural artifacts. Our parks are sanctuaries for countless species and a source of wonder for millions of visitors. They deserve our fiercest protection to preserve their ecological and cultural integrity and ensure our children and grandchildren can enjoy them for many years to come. **At the Jane Fonda Climate PAC, we’re dedicated to electing leaders who understand the urgency of protecting these treasures. We support candidates who champion robust environmental policies and oppose fossil fuel interests that jeopardize our public lands.** This Earth Month, your support can empower our mission like never before. By getting involved — whether through volunteering with our endorsed candidates, making a donation, or spreading the word about our crucial work on social media — you're helping to elect climate champions who will protect and preserve our public lands for generations to come. | [**DONATE**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/83595782/468899333/2105508926?refcode=ea.e98b1ec6-bf01-ef11-aaf0-7c1e5214dad0&ms=ea.e98b1ec6-bf01-ef11-aaf0-7c1e5214dad0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU5OGIxZWM2LWJmMDEtZWYxMS1hYWYwLTdjMWU1MjE0ZGFkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=EZy_Ljip_8MFRLE2Ss-mLOQe619B9MiphzEhbt5BI94=)

subject: No two sides of the truth
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jena for Colorado
body:
https://jenaforcolorado.com/ [https://jenaforcolorado.com/]
Friends –
Earlier this month, Colorado House Republicans attempted and failed to impeach me for calling Trump what he is: an oath-breaking insurrectionist. There is nothing political in me saying that. There are not two sides of the truth. There are not two sides to what we saw at the United States Capitol on January 6.
This impeachment attempt was the next step in their long line of conspiracy theories and political games. Let me be clear: these far-right tactics will not get in the way of me doing the job that Colorado voters elected me to do, which is to protect our Constitution and our democracy.
This sham impeachment proceeding was dismissed, and I am more committed than ever to continuing to fight for Coloradans to have their voices heard and their votes counted in our elections. I will continue this important work and remain focused on the values of my constituents.
While the far-right plays political theater, I’ll be working hard to strengthen our democracy and protect the will of the people.
Best,
Jena Griswold

body:
When we got word that Kari Lake had raised $1 million in one night earlier this month, we knew that represented one of the biggest threats to our campaign so far.
#

Peter:
We’re writing to ask you to make a donation — $5 or whatever you can — to start turning the tide in Arizona.
Here’s the truth:
When we got word that Kari Lake had raised $1 million in one night earlier this month, we knew that represented one of the biggest threats to our campaign so far.
It’s the first real, tangible sign that her fundraising efforts are gaining steam, and if she stays on this pace it could put our chances at victory and our control of the Senate at risk.
If we win, it’s that much more likely that we hold the Senate. But if we lose, it’s almost guaranteed that the GOP will hold the majority.
Winning or losing is going to come down to whether we have the resources we need to defeat Kari Lake.
So, we need an absolutely HUGE response today to show that we’ve got what it takes to take the lead and win in Arizona.
Our average contribution this month is around $32. But we’re lowering our request today — down to just $5. That might not seem like much against the millions Lake is raising, but with a ton of people chipping in alongside you it’s going to add up really fast.
That’s how we’ll win. Together. And it’s why we’re humbly asking:
[**Can you please make your first donation of $5 today and help us hit our goals before our deadline next week? When catastrophe hit our district, Jessica Morse didn’t turn her back. **When the news broke, she got in her car and drove 96 miles straight to the heart of the inferno and volunteered to help.** Just a year later, Jessica was appointed Deputy Secretary for Forest and Wildland Resilience at the California Natural Resources Agency, working on the frontline of California’s wildfire crisis and fast-tracking wildfire prevention efforts.
